name: performance

findings.message: For numeric ops (gt/gte/lt/lte), the `expected` operand is a template constant but is re-validated against `^-?[0-9]+$` on every cycle iteration rather than once at cycle start or template load, resulting in up to `_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX` (10) redundant regex evaluations per condition per cycle run.

The `matches` op evaluates `[[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]]` on every iteration with a pattern that is a template constant; bash does not cache compiled EREs across `=~` invocations, so the same regex is re-compiled up to `_CYCLE_ABSOLUTE_MAX` times per cycle, with the same pattern duplicated across all three evaluators (_cycle_eval_one_condition, _cycle_check_until, _cycle_check_abort_when).

Numeric ops now require two sequential `case` dispatches per evaluation (outer dispatch to the gt/gte/lt/lte group, inner dispatch to the specific op), adding a constant but unnecessary second dispatch that could be collapsed into a single `case` with four distinct arms at the top level.

reason: the performance lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
